messages.subject: Re: knitr and Beamer: get rid of extra blank lines around code and output
messages.subject_clean: knitr and Beamer: get rid of extra blank lines around code and output
messages.body_plain:
in case you still have that problem, just replace \newenvironment by \renewenvironment.
so the correct comamnd would be
\renewenvironment{knitrout}{\setlength{\topsep}{0mm}}{}

On Thursday, September 12, 2013 at 6:54:47 PM UTC+2, Bob wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I have searched the web back and forth and there are some hints on this but they did not lead to a success for me.
>
> I am writing a .Rnw beamer presentation using RStudio and knitr for weaving.
> My problem is that there is always extra blank lines between the R input and output. Looking at the .tex output, it seems to me that it is caused by the \begin{alltt} \end{alltt} environment. Is there any chance to get rid of such blank lines? They take up too much space on my slides.
>
> Many thanks!
> Bob
>
> \begin{frame}[fragile]
>   \frametitle{A matrix}
> TEST
> <<results='markup'>>=
>   A <- matrix(1:4, nrow=2)
>   A
> @
> \end{frame}
>
>
messages.body_snippet:
in case you still have that problem, just replace \newenvironment by \renewenvironment.
so the correct comamnd would be
\renewenvironment{knitrout}{\setlength{\topsep}{0mm}}{}

messages.subject: how do you change the size of the ggplot chart size in knitr markdown in pdf file
messages.subject_clean: how do you change the size of the ggplot chart size in knitr markdown in pdf file
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to use knitr and markdown to show some ggplot2 facet_wrap.

my df is something like this:

Hostname Date  Cpu
Server01   1/1/2015  4
Server01   1/2/205   5
Server01    1/3/2015  10
Server02   1/1/2015  6
Server02   1/2/205   20
Server02    1/3/2015  40

etc

If I have bunch of servers and I want to use this to show it in my pdf file:

```{r, results = 'asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE,tidy=FALSE}

        print(ggplot(df,aes(Date, Cpu, group=Hostname, colour=Hostname))+geom_line()+
        geom_smooth(method="lm", se=T, colour="blue")+
        facet_wrap(~Hostname, ncol=3)+theme_bw()+
```

I see in the pdf output that ggplot output is fixed. It prints one output per page. Is it possible to adjust the plot size so that it enlarges if there are many servers so that I can see them. Right now, the plot size is fixed and if there are bunch of servers, each server chart shrinks.

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Knitr does not work in TexMaker
messages.body_plain:
Hi Glenn,

Is this in any way specific to knitr?  El Capitan changed the location of files and some paths that broke a number of TeX distributions, AFAIK, and at least on one Mac I used basically no terminal-based usage of TeX worked after the upgrade.  Once symlinks and paths were fixed so that latex and pdflatex worked from the terminal, then things worked again.

I could be wrong as I'm not familiar with TexMaker specifically, but knitr normally just sends commands to a terminal to run (pdf)latex, so I'm not sure what you're having is a knitr specific problem.

Cheers,

Josh

1. If I use the following simple R code for spin()
library(rbokeh)
p <- figure() %>%
    ly_points(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, data = iris,
              color = Species, glyph = Species,
              hover = list(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width))

saved as test_rbokeh_log.R
and use spin:
spin("test_rbokeh_log.R")

I get a file "test_rbokeh_log.html" with no graphic.

If I use:
spin("test_rbokeh_log.R",knit=FALSE)

with which I can create a correct html by using the button "Preview HTML"
within RStudio.

2. More important: if I use my own data, i.e.
library(rbokeh)
p <- figure() %>%
    ly_points(x,y, data = mydf,
              color = z, glyph = z,
              hover = list(x, y))

where
mydf <- data.frame(x=rnorm(10,2),y=rnorm(20,4),

has been previously defined outside the script (i.e., on the console)
and use spin:

then I also get a file "test2_rbokeh_log.Rmd"
but get an error when using the button "Preview HTML"

  object 'mydf' not found
Calls: <Anonymous> ... _fseq -> freduce -> withVisible -> <Anonymous>
-> ly_points
Execution halted

The error does not come up if df is defined within the script
test2_rbokeh_log.R itself

Thanks for any clarification on this problem

Agus

messages.subject: Printing hyperlinks
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone!

I've been looking for this in google but didn't find it, maybe you can help me. I'm doing an analysis report in knitr and my data frame contains an attribute that is an URL to a WebPage.

What I'm trying to accomplish is: The printed output of each chunk of code in the HTML version to have the URL attribute like a link, so the user can easily navigate to those URLs when reviewing the report.

Is there a way to achieve this? I now that the markdown is [name](url), but what I'm trying is that the output of the chunk to be rendered as a link.

Use Case:
I have a dataframe containing "Website URL" and "Anual Visitors", If I print the top 10 most visited webpages, I want the output to have a clickable link to the site.

Thanks a lot!

Regards,

P.S: Is there a way for the url's to be clickable in RStudio console?

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Printing hyperlinks
messages.body_plain:
Here is something that works for me:

library(dplyr)
url <- c("http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com" <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>,
         "http://www.google.com" <http://www.google.com>)
sitename <- c("RMarkdown",
              "Google")
Visitors <- c(200,10000)
d <- data.frame(sitename,url,Visitors) %>%
  mutate(Sites = paste0("[", sitename, "](", url, ")")) %>%
  select(Sites, Visitors) %>%
  arrange(Visitors %>% desc)
rownames(d) <- paste0(1:nrow(d),".")
knitr::kable(d)
